title: Coefficient rescaling stabilizes polynomial multiplication kernels
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal, $d\geq0$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(d)\to R$. Assume that every permutation of the sequence of images of the $f_i$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For each integer $e>0$, there are $s_i\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that, with $T=R[X_i:i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\gamma_i=C(s_if_i)X_i$, multiplication by $\gamma_i$ and by $\gamma_i^2$ have equal kernels on $T/(\gamma_j^e:j<i)$ for every $i$. No target ring, field, flat chart, or maximal-ideal generation is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: Multiplying each term of a regular sequence by a unit preserves regularity. Induct on the list: the head remains injective and the quotient by the head is unchanged, since the principal ideals of a and ua are equal. In the source prime localization every coefficient outside p becomes a unit. This is implemented by regular_ofFn_mul_units.

For any current coefficient family, regular in every order after localization, apply the polynomial-variables theorem to obtain regularity of C(f_j)X_j over R_p. Raise preceding terms to e, leaving the current term at exponent one, using the positive-powers theorem. regular_mod_prev identifies injectivity of the current term modulo the ideal of preceding powers. The proved helper ofList_take_ofFn identifies this ideal with the explicit index-bounded span.

Put T=R[X_j] and S=C(R minus p). Polynomial base change makes R_p[X_j] a localization of T at S (Mathlib MvPolynomial.isLocalization). The quotient by the extended prefix ideal is the localization of T modulo that prefix: the quotient localization instance and isLocalizedModule_iff_isLocalization give the canonical module localization map. IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv identifies it with LocalizedModule S (T/I), preserving scalar multiplication. Thus the injectivity from the previous step gives equality of first and square kernels on the localized module. All these maps are the canonical maps; no arbitrary choice of ring or quotient is made.

T is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem, and T/I is finite as a T-module. Apply Ogoma to S, the current polynomial term, and T/I. Its exponent-one conclusion supplies an element C(t) of S; choose its coefficient preimage t outside p and replace only the current coefficient by t times that coefficient. This is the proved helper exists_factor_of_polynomial_regular.

Induct on n from zero to d, maintaining coefficient factors outside p and kernel equalities at all indices below n. Initially all factors are one. At index n, unit invariance from step 1 and local permutation regularity give the hypotheses of steps 2 through 4. Update only the n-th factor. For every earlier index both its current scalar and the entire preceding-power ideal are unchanged, so its kernel equality persists. A span equality proved by extensionality transports the new n-th equality to the updated family. At n=d all required indices are covered. The induction starts at d=0 without requiring an index, so the empty-family case is included.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_polynomial_coefficient_kernel_rescaling
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (d : ℕ) (f : Fin d → R)
    (hperm : ∀ l : List (Localization.AtPrime p),
      (List.ofFn (fun i ↦ algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p) (f i))).Perm l →
        IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime p) l)
    (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e) :
    ∃ s : Fin d → R, (∀ i, s i ∉ p) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin d)
        (x : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R ⧸ Ideal.span
          {y | ∃ j : Fin d, j.val < i.val ∧
            y = (MvPolynomial.C (s j * f j) * MvPolynomial.X j) ^ e}),
        (MvPolynomial.C (s i * f i) * MvPolynomial.X i) • x = 0 ↔
          (MvPolynomial.C (s i * f i) * MvPolynomial.X i) ^ 2 • x = 0)
